# 6. Standard parts are Assembly instances generated by Plugins

Date: 2026-11-13

## Status

Accepted

## Context

FreeShape needs catalogue fasteners that a user picks from a list and drops onto many holes at once, as Onshape's standard content does. Three things had to be settled: where the geometry comes from, what an inserted fastener is in the Assembly file, and how a Mate reaches it.

Geometry. Shipping vendor STEP files was the first idea. McMaster-Carr's terms bar redistributing its CAD models, making derivatives and keeping copies, and the other vendor portals checked say the same. The FreeCAD Fasteners workbench (LGPL-2.1, about 220 types) generates fasteners from dimension tables and already selects several circular edges or a face of holes. bd_warehouse (Apache-2.0) covers far fewer types and needs build123d. BOLTS is dormant. A folder of STEP files with a sidecar file for connectors would have needed a new format, and OpenCASCADE's STEP importer drops named coordinate frames.

What an instance is. A Python feature is a Part Studio feature, and a Plugin supplied only those. A fastener made that way needs a Part Studio feature for every size and length before it can be inserted, so inserting onto twelve holes could not be one action. Onshape inserts standard content straight into an Assembly.

How a Mate reaches it. A Mate end today is a picked face or edge, stored as an index with a geometric signature and re-found after the part changes. A fastener that changes length would lose or mis-find those picks.

Whether to store shapes. Python features keep their last built shape so a file opens when its Plugin is missing. A plain-shank fastener rebuilds in milliseconds, and an Assembly can hold hundreds.

## Decision

A Standard part is an instance in an Assembly with its own source kind. The Assembly records the Plugin's id and version, the part type and its parameters. It has no Part Studio and is never Published output.

A Plugin supplies Standard part types through its manifest, beside its Python features. The fasteners ship as a bundled Plugin whose generators and tables are ported from the FreeCAD Fasteners workbench.

A Standard part offers named mate connectors, computed from the same dimensions as its shape. A Mate end can hold a connector name instead of a picked face or edge. Every connector's Z points out of the face it sits on.

The Assembly stores no shape for a Standard part. Shapes are rebuilt on load. An instance made by a different version of its Plugin rebuilds with the installed one and carries a marker until the user accepts it. An instance whose Plugin or type is missing stays in the file, unresolved.

Inserting onto several holes makes one independent instance and one fastened Mate per hole. Nothing groups them.

## Consequences

- The Assembly file format gains a source kind and a connector kind, and joins the migration chain. An older FreeShape refuses the newer file.
- Mates to a Standard part survive a change of size or length, because the name is looked up again.
- The named connector kind is the one Part Studio mate connectors need. Whichever lands second adopts the first's format.
- A file that uses a Plugin the reader lacks shows nothing for those instances. Python features, which keep their last shape, behave differently. Storing shapes for Standard parts later would be an addition to the format.
- A corrected dimension table changes existing assemblies when they are next opened. The version marker is the only notice, so the Plugin version must rise whenever geometry changes.
- A Standard part cannot be used inside a Part Studio, for example to cut clearance round a bolt head. That would need the same generator offered as a Python feature.
- Because instances are independent, a hole pattern that grows gets no new fasteners until the user inserts again.
- Fastener geometry in FreeShape is LGPL-2.1 code and data inside a GPL-3.0-or-later program, with the workbench credited in the third-party notices.
- Sizes no standard lists are table rows keyed in from a supplier datasheet, so their accuracy rests on that datasheet and cannot be checked against FreeCAD.
